title: Derived pullback of a perfect complex is perfect
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $K$ be a perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] of $A$-modules. Then $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ is a perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] of $B$-modules. Here derived tensor is the fixed-second-factor functor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] evaluated at the regular $B$-module in degree zero.

proof.text: By the affine characterization [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] (Stacks Tag 08EB, with the ring form of a perfect complex, More on Algebra Definition 0656), the perfect A-complex K is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex P^\bullet of finite projective A-modules. Each P^n is projective, so Tor_i^A(P^n,B)=0 for i>0 (elementary); hence by [lem-pc-termwise-tor-acyclic-derived-tensor] the canonical map K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\cong P^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\to P^\bullet\otimes_A B is a quasi-isomorphism, so the derived tensor is represented by the ordinary termwise tensor complex.

Each P^n is a direct summand of a finite free A-module A^m, so P^n\otimes_A B is a direct summand of A^m\otimes_A B=B^m, i.e. finite projective over B (elementary). Hence P^\bullet\otimes_A B is a bounded complex of finite projective B-modules, so by the converse direction of [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] (over Spec B) it is a perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-complex] of B-modules.
